anchors.quote: I have told Murray to send you by post (if possible) a copy of my book

groups.interpretation: Darwin told Murray to send Wallace a copy if possible.
groups.boundary_reason: The instruction and hope of receipt do not establish an actual delivery date.

questions.direct: Who arranged for Wallace to receive Darwin’s book, and whom did he ask to send it?
questions.paraphrase: In Darwin’s letter to Wallace, who set up the book shipment and who was supposed to post it?
questions.boundary: On what date did Wallace actually receive the copy arranged in Darwin’s letter?

groups.interpretation: Huxley reports finishing his reading the previous day.
groups.boundary_reason: A report of reading does not date public release.

questions.direct: What does Huxley say he finished the previous day in his November 23 letter to Darwin?
questions.paraphrase: In the November 23 note to Darwin, what had Huxley just finished doing?
questions.boundary: From Huxley’s November 23 note alone, on what date was Darwin’s book publicly released?

anchors.quote: employed in correcting for second edition of 3000 copies

groups.interpretation: The diary describes corrections for a second edition of 3,000 copies.
groups.boundary_reason: The note names the edition and planned number of copies without listing revised sentences.

questions.direct: According to the diary entry, which edition was Darwin correcting at the end of November and beginning of December?
questions.paraphrase: What edition does the diary say Darwin was preparing corrections for around the turn from November to December?
questions.boundary: Which exact sentences did Darwin rewrite according to that diary entry?

anchors.quote: We hold these truths to be sacred & undeniable
We hold these truths to be self-evident

groups.interpretation: The opening uses sacred & undeniable in the draft and self-evident in the final version.
groups.boundary_reason: The wording comparison does not identify the person responsible.

questions.direct: Compare the opening truth claim in Jefferson’s rough draft and the final Declaration transcript. How did the description of the truths change?
questions.paraphrase: How did the opening description of the truths shift from Jefferson’s draft to the final Declaration?
questions.boundary: Which individual personally chose the final wording, as proven solely by the two opening passages?

anchors.quote: the Confederate batteries opened fire on the fort
Major Anderson surrendered Fort Sumter, evacuating the garrison on the following day
announcing his withdrawal from Fort Sumter; April 18, 1861

groups.interpretation: Source narration gives April 12 firing, April 13 surrender, evacuation the following day and an April 18 catalogue date.
groups.boundary_reason: Catalogue, relay, narration and event dates do not prove receipt time.

questions.direct: Distinguish the bombardment, surrender, evacuation and telegram dates in the Fort Sumter record.
questions.paraphrase: What separate dates does the Fort Sumter page give for opening fire, giving up the fort, leaving it, and the telegram date listed in the catalogue?
questions.boundary: What exact minute did the recipient receive the Fort Sumter telegram according to the cited dates?

anchors.quote: was aborted because of an abrupt loss of service module cryogenic oxygen

groups.interpretation: The report attributes the abort to abrupt cryogenic oxygen loss associated with a tank fire.
groups.boundary_reason: The report’s causal description supplies no named authorizer.

questions.direct: According to the Apollo 13 mission report summary, what loss caused the lunar landing to be aborted?
questions.paraphrase: What did the Apollo 13 report say was lost, leading the crew to abandon its planned landing?
questions.boundary: Who authorized the fire that the Apollo 13 summary mentions?

anchors.quote: full blame should the effort to create a beachhead on the Normandy coast fail

groups.interpretation: Eisenhower prepared a note that would accept blame if the operation failed.
groups.boundary_reason: The publication condition is not evidence that the event occurred.

questions.direct: What condition did Eisenhower put on accepting full blame in the note intended for release?
questions.paraphrase: In the archives’ account of his note, under what circumstances would Eisenhower take full blame?
questions.boundary: Which actual defeat does the contingent blame note itself establish?

anchors.quote: and which excepted parts, are for the present, left precisely as if this proclamation were not issued

groups.interpretation: Excepted areas were for the present treated as if the proclamation had not been issued.
groups.boundary_reason: The clause describes its own scope without naming a later law.

questions.direct: What does the Emancipation Proclamation say about the status of the excepted parts?
questions.paraphrase: How did the proclamation say the areas it carved out would be treated for the time being?
questions.boundary: Which later law removed every exception, as established by the exception clause alone?

anchors.quote: Ferdinand Hayden surveyed the area in 1871

groups.interpretation: The archive’s introductory narrative attributes the 1871 survey to Ferdinand Hayden.
groups.boundary_reason: The supporting statement is archival framing, not the act.

questions.direct: According to the archive’s introductory narrative, who surveyed Yellowstone in 1871?
questions.paraphrase: Whom does the archival introduction credit with the 1871 Yellowstone survey?
questions.boundary: Which provision in the Yellowstone law itself names Hayden as the surveyor?

anchors.quote: The Secretary may in his discretion, grant leases for building purposes for terms not exceeding ten years

groups.interpretation: The law gives discretionary authority to grant building leases for at most ten years.
groups.boundary_reason: Authorization and duration do not establish that a lease was actually granted.

questions.direct: What discretion and maximum term does the Yellowstone act give the Secretary for building leases?
questions.paraphrase: Under the Yellowstone law, must the Secretary issue building leases, and how long can those leases last?
questions.boundary: Which named visitor actually received a ten-year lease under the quoted Yellowstone provision?
